thread:
maria-ops: Heads up — EU GPU nodepools failed to provision after chart bump. Pods ended up on cpu nodes, autoscaler didn't pick GPU nodes, and we saw a provisioning delay/cost spike.

jonathan-platform: Can you paste the rendered pod/PodSpec affinity from the manifest? suspect templating weirdness (toYaml + quote?)

maria-ops: Here's the values snippet we pushed yesterday and the rendered portion.

values.yaml (we set affinity under workloads):
```
affinity:
  nodeAffinity:
    requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
      nodeSelectorTerms:
        - matchExpressions:
            - key: "kubernetes.io/gpu"
              operator: In
              values: ["true"]
```

chart helper we used (helpers/_affinity.tpl):
```
{{- define "infra.affinity" -}}
{{ toYaml .Values.affinity | quote }}
{{- end -}}
```

rendered manifest snippet in cluster (what kubernetes received):
```
affinity: \"nodeAffinity:\\n  requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:\\n    nodeSelectorTerms:\\n      - matchExpressions:\\n          - key: \\\"kubernetes.io/gpu\\\"\\n            operator: In\\n            values: [\\\"true\\\"]\\n\"
```

kai-templates: This is the classic "toYaml + quote" trap. toYaml produces a YAML block/string; piping to | quote wraps the entire block in quotes, so Helm emits a string value for affinity. K8s expects an object — autoscaler and scheduler ignore the string.

alex-eng: Fix is to stop quoting and use nindent to keep indentation, e.g.:
```
{{- define "infra.affinity" -}}
{{ toYaml .Values.affinity | nindent 8 }}
{{- end -}}
```
Or if you need a single-line JSON blob in an annotation use toJson.

maria-ops: Another contributing factor — our CI has a lint step that runs a small transform (envsubst) on values for feature flags; an earlier change caused object values to be serialized into strings before template rendering in the release pipeline. So we have two issues: the helper and a pipeline stage.

jonathan-platform: Add a schema guard to values.schema.json to catch when affinity becomes a string. Example rule:
```
"properties": {
  "affinity": { "type": ["object", "null"] }
}
```
Fail fast in chart lint if affinity is not an object.

kai-templates: I'll open a PR with the helper change + helm-unittest case that renders the chart and asserts the affinity block is emitted unquoted. Quick patch:
```
- {{ toYaml .Values.affinity | quote }}
+ {{- if .Values.affinity }}
+ {{ toYaml .Values.affinity | nindent 8 }}
+ {{- end }}
```

infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout started for chart infra-gpu v2.1.4 -> eu-cluster (3 pods)

sre-oncall: Noted. We saw a CPU node autoscale spike yesterday ~08:00–16:00 UTC while GPU pods waited. Cost impact ~$1.2k for the window. Added alert to watch for "k8s.pod.affinity_is_string" and a runbook note.

maria-ops: PR opened: https://git.company/repo/charts/infra-gpu/pulls/4321 — includes helper fix, schema update, and unit test. Rolling to canary now; if green we'll promote. Temporary workaround: pin nodeSelector: { "kubernetes.io/gpu": "true" } in values to force scheduling to GPU pool until fix promotes.

jonathan-platform: :thumbsup: Also add a CI lint check that greps rendered manifests for affinity: " and fails if found — cheap guard until schema + tests catch it.

kai-templates: Will land the change and add the helm unittest and chart-lint rule. Thanks for catching it early, maria.

maria-ops: Thanks all — monitoring and costs team will follow up with a short postmortem if the rollback is needed. Keep me posted.
